mainTopic: The end of the sugya on the מעלה for קדשים, then the משנה and גמרא on which grains and produce can be used for מצה, and which dough brings כרת as חמץ
overview: This amud opens by finishing a sugya about consecrated liquids that became impure. The גמרא explains that the rule against purifying them is only a מעלה, an extra stringency the Sages added for holy things. רב שימי בר אשי and רב אשי each bring another source showing such a מעלה. Then a new משנה begins. It lists the five grains that can be used for מצה, which kinds of produce may and may not be used, and the case of breads baked for a תודה or a נזיר. The גמרא identifies the grains. It learns from a פסוק that only something that can become חמץ can be מצה, so rice and millet are excluded. It then shows that רבי יוחנן בן נורי disagrees, holding that rice is a real grain, and adds his ruling about קרמית. Finally, the students of רב אידי בר אבין debate why ריש לקיש says dough kneaded with wine, oil, or honey brings no כרת. רב אידי wakes up and begins to explain that these are מי פירות, and his explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The previous proof ends: it is only a higher standard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the earlier proof by saying the rule is just a מעלה, and the same applies to our case of impure קדשים liquids.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is a higher standard. Here too, it is a higher standard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a proof it started on the previous amud. It says the earlier rule was only an extra stringency, and our case of impure קדשים liquids is the same kind of extra stringency.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier source showed a rule that is stricter than Torah law requires. The גמרא explains that this was a מעלה, an extra stringency the Sages added. It then applies the same idea here: the rule that impure קדשים liquids cannot be purified is also only a מעלה.

keyTerms.meaning: A higher standard; an extra stringency the Sages added, especially for holy things

steps.confusionAlert: Calling this a מעלה does not mean the liquid stops being impure or stops being holy. It means the extra strictness comes from the Sages, not from the Torah.

phrases.english: Rather, it is a higher standard.
phrases.notes: So the earlier source was just being stricter than Torah law requires.

phrases.english: So too here, it is a higher standard.
phrases.notes: Applies that idea to impure קדשים liquids.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the proof that began on the previous amud.
steps.raayaObject: That the rule for impure קדשים liquids is a rabbinic מעלה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The earlier source (on the previous amud) where the Sages made a rule stricter than the Torah requires

steps.title: רב שימי בר אשי quotes a ברייתא about someone who immersed
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר אשי brings another source: a person who immersed may eat מעשר right away, and may eat תרומה after nightfall.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר אשי said: We also learned this. If he immersed and came up, he may eat מעשר. Once his sun has set, he may eat תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי בר אשי starts a second proof by quoting a ברייתא. This step only gives the source; the next step draws the point from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא sets up steps of purity: right after immersing, a person may eat מעשר. After nightfall, he may eat תרומה. The ברייתא does not mention קדשים at this level, and that silence is what the next step builds on.

keyTerms.meaning: We too have learned it; introduces a source that supports the point
He immersed and came up from the מקוה
Tithe (here, מעשר שני, which has a lighter purity level)
His sun has set; nightfall after immersion completes purification
The כהן's portion, which needs a higher level of purity

phrases.english: Rav Shimi bar Ashi said:
We too have learned this:
If he immersed and came up, he may eat tithe.
Once his sun has set, he may eat תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate proof for the same idea of a מעלה.
steps.raayaObject: That the Sages set a מעלה for קדשים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about stages of purity after immersion

steps.title: Inference: תרומה yes, קדשים no — but he is already pure
steps.stepSummary: From the ברייתא we see he may eat תרומה but not קדשים. The גמרא asks why, since he is already fully pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: For תרומה, yes. For קדשים, no. Why? He is pure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the ברייתא closely: it allows תרומה but leaves out קדשים. It then asks why קדשים should still be forbidden if the person is already pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After nightfall, the person counts as טהור. So by basic purity rules he should be allowed to eat everything. The fact that קדשים is still held back shows that something beyond basic purity is at work. The question is rhetorical and sets up the answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Consecrated food, such as sacrificial meat

phrases.english: With תרומה, yes; with consecrated food, no.
phrases.notes: We figure this out from what the ברייתא doesn't mention.

phrases.english: Why? He is pure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the key point out of the ברייתא quoted in step 2.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If he is fully טהור after nightfall, there should be no reason to forbid קדשים.

steps.title: Answer: it is a higher standard, and so too here
steps.stepSummary: The reason קדשים is held back is a מעלה. In the same way, impure קדשים liquids are a מעלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is a higher standard. Here too, it is a higher standard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question: holding back קדשים is a מעלה, an extra stringency. That supports the claim that the rule about impure קדשים liquids is also a מעלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows that the Sages treat קדשים more strictly even when a person is technically pure. That gives a real example of a מעלה for קדשים. It strengthens the main claim about consecrated liquids.

keyTerms.meaning: So too here; applies the conclusion to the case under discussion

steps.whatToRemember: רב שימי בר אשי's proof: a person who is already pure still may not eat קדשים, which shows the Sages added a מעלה for holy things.

phrases.english: Rather, it is a higher standard.
So too here, it is a higher standard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the extra restriction as a rabbinic stringency
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Someone who is טהור should be allowed to eat קדשים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Holding back קדשים is a מעלה, and the same applies to impure קדשים liquids.

steps.title: רב אשי quotes a teaching that includes wood and frankincense
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי brings a third source: the word "והבשר" in the verse comes to include the Temple wood and frankincense.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: We also learned this. "And the flesh" comes to include the wood and the frankincense.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי opens a third proof by quoting a teaching on a verse about impure sacrificial meat. This step only sets up the source; the next step shows what is surprising about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse in ויקרא speaks about holy meat that touched something impure. The extra word "והבשר" is read as including the wood for the מזבח and the לבונה. So these too are treated as able to become impure.

keyTerms.meaning: "And the flesh"; the word in the verse that is expanded
To include; a word in the verse that adds more cases
Wood (for the fire on the מזבח)

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
We too have learned this:
"And the flesh" comes to include the wood and the frankincense.
phrases.notes: This comes from the פסוק in ויקרא ז:יט.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי, אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third, separate proof for the idea of a מעלה.
steps.raayaObject: That the Sages set a מעלה for holy things
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching that "והבשר" includes wood and frankincense

steps.title: Can wood and frankincense even become impure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that wood and frankincense are not food, so normally they cannot become impure at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can wood and frankincense become impure?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a sharp rhetorical question about the source: wood and frankincense are not food or drink, so how can they become impure? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally only foods, drinks, and certain vessels can receive impurity. Wood and frankincense do not fit those categories. So treating them as impure must come from something other than the basic rules.

keyTerms.meaning: Things that are able to become impure

phrases.english: Are wood and frankincense things that can become impure?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the source quoted in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The teaching that includes wood and frankincense
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Things that are not food or drink cannot normally become impure.

steps.title: Answer: a higher standard, and the same here
steps.stepSummary: Wood and frankincense are treated as impure only because of a מעלה, and the same is true of impure קדשים liquids.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is a higher standard. Here too, it is a higher standard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that wood and frankincense are treated as impure only because of a מעלה for holy things. It then applies the same idea to the case of impure קדשים liquids.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since basic purity law cannot explain the rule, it must be an extra stringency based on holiness. This is the third example of a מעלה for holy things. All three proofs support the same claim about consecrated liquids.
steps.whatToRemember: Three proofs (the earlier one, רב שימי בר אשי's, and רב אשי's) all show that the Sages added a מעלה for holy things. That is why impure קדשים liquids cannot be purified.

phrases.english: Rather, it is a higher standard.
Here too, it is a higher standard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 6 and closes the sugya.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the rule as a rabbinic stringency
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Wood and frankincense cannot become impure at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are treated as impure because of a מעלה, and so are impure קדשים liquids.

steps.title: New משנה: the five grains that can be used for מצה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists five grains that can be used to fulfill the obligation of eating מצה on פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are the grains with which a person fulfills his obligation on פסח: wheat, barley, spelt, rye, and oats.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. The משנה lists the five grains whose מצה counts for the מצוה on פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only these five grains count. Other foods, like rice or millet, do not. The גמרא will later connect this to the rule that only grains that can become חמץ can be used for מצה.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; marks the start of a new משנה

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the halacha that מצה must be made from one of the five grains.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
These are the things with which a person fulfills
his obligation on Passover:
with wheat, with barley, with spelt,
and with rye and with oats.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵלּוּ דְּבָרִים שֶׁאָדָם יוֹצֵא בָּהֶן יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ בַּפֶּסַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unrelated to the previous sugya.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מצה made from the five grains fulfills the obligation.

steps.title: Produce with uncertain or special status can also be used
steps.stepSummary: One may also use דמאי, מעשר ראשון whose תרומה was taken, and redeemed מעשר שני or הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one fulfills it with doubtfully tithed produce, with first tithe whose תרומה was taken, and with second tithe and consecrated property that were redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds that even produce with a special or doubtful status can be used for מצה, as long as it is permitted to eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דמאי is only a rabbinic doubt, so it still counts. מעשר ראשון is fine once its תרומת מעשר was removed. מעשר שני and הקדש count only after they were redeemed; before that, they have restrictions that make them unfit.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce bought from an עם הארץ, where it is uncertain whether it was tithed
The first tithe, given to the לוי
The second tithe, eaten in ירושלים or redeemed
Property consecrated to the בית המקדש

steps.confusionAlert: The word "redeemed" (שנפדו) refers to מעשר שני and הקדש. Unredeemed מעשר שני or הקדש would not work.

phrases.english: And one fulfills it with doubtfully tithed produce,
and with first tithe whose תרומה was taken,
and with second tithe and consecrated property that were redeemed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה by listing what kinds of produce are acceptable.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Permitted produce with special status (דמאי, fixed מעשר ראשון, redeemed מעשר שני and הקדש) fulfills the obligation.

steps.title: כהנים may use חלה and תרומה
steps.stepSummary: כהנים may fulfill the obligation with מצה made from חלה or תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the priests may fulfill it with חלה and with תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends this section by saying that כהנים, who are allowed to eat חלה and תרומה, may use them for their מצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a כהן is permitted to eat חלה and תרומה, these count as "his" food for the מצוה. A non-כהן could not use them, because he may not eat them.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of dough given to the כהן

phrases.english: And the priests with חלה and with תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a special case for כהנים to the משנה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כהנים fulfill the מצה obligation with חלה and תרומה.

steps.title: Forbidden produce cannot be used for מצה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists the produce that does NOT work for מצה: טבל, מעשר ראשון whose תרומה was not taken, and מעשר שני or הקדש that was not redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a person cannot fulfill his obligation with untithed produce, with first tithe whose תרומה was not separated, or with second tithe or consecrated grain that was not redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives the other side of its list. Step 9 said which produce does work, and this step says which produce does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case here matches a case from step 9, but this time the needed step was never done: no tithing, no separating תרומה, or no redemption. Since the produce is still forbidden to eat, it cannot be used for the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce from which תרומה and מעשרות have not yet been separated. It is forbidden to eat.
The second tithe. It must be eaten in ירושלים or redeemed with money.
Property consecrated to the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: But not with untithed produce,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא בְּמַעֲשֵׂר רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁלֹּא נִטְּלָה תְּרוּמָתוֹ,
phrases.english: nor with first tithe whose terumah was not taken,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא בְּמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי וְהֶקְדֵּשׁ שֶׁלֹּא נִפְדּוּ.
phrases.english: nor with second tithe or consecrated grain that were not redeemed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposite side of the list in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Produce that is still forbidden to eat (טבל, untithed מעשר ראשון, unredeemed מעשר שני or הקדש) cannot be used for the מצוה of מצה.

steps.title: Thanksgiving loaves and nazirite wafers
steps.stepSummary: The breads of a תודה and the wafers of a נזיר do not work for מצה if a person made them for his own offering. They do work if a baker made them to sell in the market.
steps.simpleTranslation: מצה loaves of a תודה offering and wafers of a נזיר: if he made them for himself, one does not fulfill the obligation with them. If he made them to sell in the market, one does fulfill the obligation with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a final, special case: breads that are baked as part of a קרבן. Whether they count for מצה depends on why they were made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone baking these breads for his own קרבן is preparing them only for the offering, not for the מצוה of מצה. A market baker is not sure they will sell, so he has in mind that he might use them as regular מצה. The גמרא explains this difference later.

keyTerms.meaning: The מצה loaves brought along with a קרבן תודה (thanksgiving offering).
The thin מצה wafers that a נזיר brings at the end of his נזירות.
He made them for himself, meaning for his own offering.

steps.confusionAlert: The breads themselves are the same in both cases. The only difference is the baker's purpose when he made them.

phrases.english: Loaves of the thanksgiving offering and wafers of a nazirite,
if he made them for himself, one does not fulfill the obligation with them.
If he made them to sell in the market, one does fulfill the obligation with them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new case about bread made for a קרבן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Breads of a תודה or נזיר made for one's own offering do not count for מצה. Breads made to sell in the market do count.

steps.title: Identifying the five grains
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא sorts the five grains into two families. כוסמין is a kind of wheat, and שיבולת שועל and שיפון are kinds of barley. It also gives their everyday Aramaic names.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: spelt is a type of wheat, and oats and rye are types of barley. Spelt is called גולבא, rye is called דישרא, and oats are called שבילי תעלא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by explaining the less familiar grain names from the משנה in step 8. It groups them and translates them into common Aramaic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that the five grains are really two families: wheat and barley. The Aramaic names help the learner know exactly which plants are meant.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught. This introduces a ברייתא.
Usually translated as oats, a type of barley.

phrases.english: GEMARA. It was taught: spelt is a type of wheat,
oats and rye are a type of barley.
Spelt is gulba, rye is dishra,
oats are shevilei ta'ala.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the grain names listed in the משנה in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The five grains are two families: wheat (with spelt) and barley (with oats and rye).

steps.title: Rice and millet are excluded
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws the result: only these five grains work, and אורז and דוחן do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: These, yes. Rice and millet, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the practical result of the list: rice and millet cannot be used for מצה. This sets up the next question, which asks for the source of this rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rice and millet look like grains, so a learner might think they should count. The גמרא makes clear that the list is closed. This short line leads straight into the question of where the rule comes from.

phrases.english: These, yes. Rice and millet, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical result from the list of grains.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the five grains can be used for מצה. אורז and דוחן cannot.

steps.title: What is the source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that limits מצה to these grains and excludes rice and millet.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where are these matters derived?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule from step 14. This line sets up the answer that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack on the rule. It is a request for the פסוק that the rule is based on.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these matters derived? This is a request for a source.

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the exclusion in step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source showing that only the five grains, and not rice or millet, can be used for מצה.

steps.title: Only what can become חמץ can be מצה
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן לקיש, the school of רבי ישמעאל, and the school of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב all derive the rule from a פסוק. Because the פסוק places חמץ and מצה side by side, only grains that can become חמץ can be used for מצה. Rice and millet do not become חמץ. They just spoil.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש said, and the school of רבי ישמעאל and the school of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב taught the same: the verse says, "Do not eat חמץ with it; seven days you shall eat מצות with it." Things that can become חמץ are the things one can use for מצה. This excludes rice and millet, which do not become חמץ but only rot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 15 with a פסוק from דברים. Three separate sources agree on the same explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links the ban on חמץ directly to the מצוה of מצה. So the מצה must come from something that could have become חמץ if it were not watched. Rice and millet only rot, so they can never be חמץ, and therefore they can never be מצה either.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in the school of.

steps.whatToRemember: The basic rule is that only something that can become חמץ can be used for מצה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle sets the limits of the מצוה. It is also the background for the later debate with רבי יוחנן בן נורי.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said,
and so taught the school of Rabbi Yishmael,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב:
phrases.english: and so taught the school of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov:
The verse says: "Do not eat chametz with it;
seven days you shall eat matzot with it."
Things that can come to leavening,

phrases.aramaic: אָדָם יוֹצֵא בָּהֶן יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ בְּמַצָּה,
phrases.english: with them a person fulfills his obligation of matzah.

phrases.aramaic: יָצְאוּ אֵלּוּ שֶׁאֵין בָּאִין לִידֵי חִימּוּץ,
phrases.english: This excludes these, which do not come to leavening,
but rather to rotting.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא לֹא תֹאכַל עָלָיו חָמֵץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question from step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק links חמץ and מצה, so only grains that can become חמץ qualify for מצה. Rice and millet only rot, so they are excluded.

steps.title: The משנה disagrees with רבי יוחנן בן נורי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the משנה does not follow רבי יוחנן בן נורי. He holds that rice is a real grain and that one is liable to כרת for eating it as חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה is not like רבי יוחנן בן נורי, who said: rice is a type of grain, and one is liable to כרת for eating it leavened.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a תנא who disagrees with the משנה. In his view, rice can become real חמץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the principle in step 16, if rice can become חמץ, it could also be used for מצה. So the משנה's exclusion of rice must follow the view that rice cannot become חמץ, not the view of רבי יוחנן בן נורי.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה is not according to.
The punishment of being cut off, given for eating חמץ on פסח.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי,
phrases.english: Our mishnah is not like Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri,
who said: rice is a type of grain,
and one is liable to karet for its leavening.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Names a תנא whose view conflicts with the exclusion of rice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה does not follow רבי יוחנן בן נורי, who considers rice a real grain whose חמץ carries כרת.

steps.title: Source for רבי יוחנן בן נורי's view
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports the attribution in step 17. רבי יוחנן בן נורי forbids rice and millet on פסח because they come close to becoming חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי יוחנן בן נורי forbids rice and millet, because they are close to becoming leavened.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא where רבי יוחנן בן נורי forbids rice and millet on פסח. This is the source for attributing a different view to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows that רבי יוחנן בן נורי forbids rice and millet on פסח, which conflicts with the משנה's exclusion of rice. His stated reason is that they are 'close to becoming חמץ.' Whether that means real חמץ is exactly the question the גמרא asks in step 19, and step 20 answers it.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the later אשכנזי custom of קטניות. Here we are dealing with a real disagreement among the תנאים about whether rice can become actual חמץ.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי אוֹסֵר בְּאוֹרֶז וְדוֹחַן
phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri forbids rice and millet
because they are close to becoming leavened.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי אוֹסֵר בְּאוֹרֶז וְדוֹחַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source for the view attributed to רבי יוחנן בן נורי in step 17.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוחנן בן נורי disagrees with the משנה and forbids rice and millet on פסח.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי יוחנן בן נורי forbids rice and millet because they are close to becoming חמץ.

steps.title: What does 'close to becoming חמץ' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי יוחנן בן נורי's phrase 'close to becoming חמץ' means rice becomes חמץ even faster than other grains, or that it only resembles חמץ without being real חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: what does 'close to becoming חמץ' mean? Does it mean that it becomes חמץ quickly? Or maybe it means it is only 'close' to חמץ, but it never becomes full חמץ?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבי יוחנן בן נורי meant in the ברייתא from step 18. It offers two possible readings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading one: rice really becomes חמץ, and it even does so quickly. That would mean real חמץ and real כרת. Reading two: rice only looks like חמץ, so the ban is a precaution, and there is no כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked by the scholars
That it comes early, meaning it happens faster

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'close' does not mean 'nearly happens'. In the first reading it means 'quick to happen'.

phrases.english: They asked:
"That it is close to becoming leavened" — what does it mean?
That it leavens early (faster than other grains)?
Or perhaps: "close to leavening" it is,
but full-fledged חמץ it is not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the key phrase in the ברייתא of step 18 means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבי יוחנן בן נורי hold that rice becomes real חמץ, which brings כרת, or only something that resembles חמץ?

steps.title: Rice is a real grain for רבי יוחנן בן נורי
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי יוחנן בן נורי calls rice a real grain. Its חמץ brings כרת, and one fulfills מצה with it. So 'close to becoming חמץ' means it becomes חמץ quickly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear a ברייתא. רבי יוחנן בן נורי said: Rice is a kind of grain. One is liable to כרת for eating it as חמץ, and a person fulfills his obligation of מצה with it on פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a ברייתא. It shows that רבי יוחנן בן נורי treats rice as a full grain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If eating rice חמץ brings כרת, then rice must become real חמץ. That proves the first reading: 'close to becoming חמץ' means it becomes חמץ quickly. This fits the rule from step 16: a grain that can become חמץ can also be used for מצה.

keyTerms.meaning: Spiritual cutting-off, the punishment for eating חמץ on פסח

steps.whyThisMatters: It ties together the חמץ side and the מצה side. For רבי יוחנן בן נורי, rice counts fully on both.

phrases.english: Come and hear, as it was taught in a ברייתא:
Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri said:
Rice is a type of grain,
and one is liable to כרת for its leavened form,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָדָם יוֹצֵא בּוֹ יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ בַּפֶּסַח.
phrases.english: and a person fulfills his obligation with it on פסח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the question of step 19 in favor of the first reading.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Rice becomes real חמץ, and quickly. So it brings כרת and is valid for מצה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן בן נורי: קרמית requires חלה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא goes on to add another ruling of רבי יוחנן בן נורי: dough made from קרמית requires separating חלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so too רבי יוחנן בן נורי used to say: קרמית is obligated in חלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a similar ruling from the same תנא. It treats another uncommon plant as a real grain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the five grains require חלה. By requiring חלה from קרמית, רבי יוחנן בן נורי counts it as a kind of grain, just as he does with rice. The word 'וכן' (and so too) tells us that the two rulings follow the same approach.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of dough given to a כהן

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: And so too Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri would say:
Keramit is obligated in challah.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a parallel ruling from the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dough made from קרמית must have חלה separated.

steps.title: What is קרמית?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what plant the word קרמית refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is קרמית?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask what the unfamiliar word means. This sets up the definition that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We cannot understand the ruling until we know which plant it is talking about. So the גמרא pauses to define the term.

phrases.english: What is keramit?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of a word in step 21.

steps.title: אביי: it is שיצניתא
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that קרמית is the plant called שיצניתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is שיצניתא.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers by giving the local Aramaic name of the plant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He swaps the Hebrew name for the name people used in his time. But that name is also unclear, so the גמרא will ask again.

keyTerms.meaning: The local name for the wild grain

phrases.english: Abaye said: It is shitzanita.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.

steps.title: What is שיצניתא?
steps.stepSummary: Since שיצניתא is also unfamiliar, the גמרא asks what that is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is שיצניתא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question. It needs a clearer definition of אביי's word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's answer only replaced one unclear word with another. The גמרא wants a description that people can actually recognize.

phrases.english: What is shitzanita?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on אביי's answer.

steps.title: רב פפא: the grain growing among reeds
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא defines שיצניתא as the wild grain found growing between papyrus reeds.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It is the שיצניתא that is found among the reeds.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a clear description by saying where the plant grows. This finishes the definition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying where the plant grows lets people identify it. So we now know what רבי יוחנן בן נורי's חלה ruling is about.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן בן נורי gives full grain status to rice and to קרמית, a wild grain found among reeds.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
It is the shitzanita that is found among the papyrus reeds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the follow-up question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שיצניתא is the wild grain that grows among papyrus reeds.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: dough kneaded with wine, oil, or honey brings no כרת
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה quotes ריש לקיש: if dough was kneaded with wine, oil, or honey instead of water, there is no כרת for eating it as חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of ריש לקיש: Dough that was kneaded with wine, oil, or honey — one is not liable to כרת for its חמץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic. It brings a new rule about dough made with fruit juices instead of water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dough is made from a proper grain, but it was mixed with liquids other than water. ריש לקיש rules that its rising does not bring the כרת punishment. He does not give his reason yet, and that is what the next steps will look for.

keyTerms.meaning: Wine, oil, and honey (fruit liquids, not water)

steps.confusionAlert: ריש לקיש only says there is no כרת. He does not say the dough is allowed on פסח.

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said
that Reish Lakish said:
Dough that was kneaded with wine, oil, or honey —
one is not liable to כרת for its leavening.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about the liquids used to knead dough.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dough kneaded only with wine, oil, or honey does not bring כרת for its חמץ.

steps.title: The scene: students before a dozing רב אידי בר אבין
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע sat before their teacher רב אידי בר אבין, who was dozing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא and רב הונא son of רב יהושע were sitting before רב אידי בר אבין, and רב אידי בר אבין was sitting and dozing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא describes the scene where a discussion of ריש לקיש's rule took place. This sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their teacher is dozing, so the two students talk the matter over between themselves. This story frame leads into their question.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa was sitting
along with Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua
before Rav Idi bar Avin,
and Rav Idi bar Avin was sitting
and dozing.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב רַב פָּפָּא וְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the story setting for discussing step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling. This is the narrative setting for the coming discussion.

steps.title: What is ריש לקיש's reason?
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע asks רב פפא why ריש לקיש rules there is no כרת for dough kneaded with fruit liquids.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע said to רב פפא: What is the reason of ריש לקיש?
steps.whatsHappening: The student asks for the reason behind ריש לקיש's rule. This sets up the answer in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule in step 26 was given with no reason. Now the גמרא looks for the reason: why does dough made from real grain not bring כרת when it is kneaded with these liquids?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said to
Rav Pappa:
What is the reason of Reish Lakish?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the rule in step 26, within the scene of step 27.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why is there no כרת for dough kneaded with wine, oil, or honey?

steps.title: רב פפא Links חמץ to מצה
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that the פסוק connects חמץ with מצה. Only a dough that can work for the מצוה of מצה brings כרת when it becomes חמץ. Dough made with fruit liquids is מצה עשירה, so its חמץ brings no כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Because the verse says, "Do not eat חמץ with it; for seven days you shall eat מצה with it." Any dough that a person can use to fulfill the מצוה of מצה brings כרת if it becomes חמץ. This dough, made with wine, oil, or honey, cannot be used for the מצוה, because it is "rich מצה." So there is no כרת if it becomes חמץ.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers רב הונא's question from Step 28. He explains why ריש לקיש says there is no כרת for dough kneaded with fruit liquids.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts "don't eat חמץ" right next to "eat מצה." From this, רב פפא learns a matching rule: the dough that counts for מצה is the same dough that brings כרת as חמץ. Dough made with wine, oil, or honey is מצה עשירה, not the plain "poor man's bread" the Torah requires. So it is outside the match on both sides.

keyTerms.meaning: "Because the verse says". This introduces a source from the תורה.
Fulfilling one's obligation (here, the מצוה of eating מצה).
"Rich מצה": dough made with wine, oil, or honey instead of water. It cannot be used for the מצוה.

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a two-sided rule: whatever can be מצה is what can bring כרת as חמץ. The next step tests this rule.

phrases.english: He (Rav Pappa) said to him: Because the verse says:
"You shall not eat leavened bread with it, etc."
phrases.notes: The פסוק goes on: "seven days you shall eat מצה with it" (דברים טז:ג), putting חמץ and מצה side by side.

phrases.english: Things with which a person fulfills
his obligation of matza,
one is liable to karet for eating them leavened.
But this dough, since a person does not
fulfill his obligation with it,
because it is considered "rich matza",
one is not liable to karet for eating it leavened.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question asked in Step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק links חמץ to מצה. Dough that cannot work as מצה (מצה עשירה) brings no כרת as חמץ.

steps.title: Challenge from Dissolved and Swallowed Bread
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע challenges רב פפא with a ברייתא. If someone dissolves a baked item and swallows it, he gets כרת if it was חמץ, but does not fulfill the מצוה if it was מצה. So the link between מצה and חמץ breaks.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע challenged רב פפא: We learned that if someone dissolved a baked item and swallowed it, then if it is חמץ he is punished with כרת, and if it is מצה he does not fulfill his obligation on פסח. But here is a case where a person does not fulfill his obligation of מצה, and still one gets כרת for its חמץ!
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא brings a ברייתא that seems to contradict רב פפא's rule. It shows a case where something does not work for מצה but still brings כרת as חמץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא's rule says the two always go together: no מצה means no כרת. The ברייתא shows a case where they split apart. Dissolved and swallowed מצה does not count for the מצוה, yet dissolved and swallowed חמץ does bring כרת. So the link cannot be a full, two-sided rule.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged him from a תנאי source (משנה or ברייתא).
He dissolved it (soaked it in liquid until it fell apart).
He swallowed it (gulped it down instead of eating normally).

steps.confusionAlert: The reason dissolved מצה does not work is the way it is eaten (gulping is not normal eating). It is not about the dough's ingredients. Still, the challenge is valid: the ברייתא shows that "no מצה" does not always mean "no כרת."

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְרַב פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, challenged Rav Pappa:
If he dissolved it and swallowed it,
if it is leavened bread, he is punished with karet;
and if it is matza,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אָדָם יוֹצֵא יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ בַּפֶּסַח.
phrases.english: a person does not fulfill his obligation on Passover.
But here is a case where a person does not fulfill
his obligation of matza,
and yet one is liable to karet for its leavened state?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְרַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the matching rule רב פפא proposed in Step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's rule that only what works as מצה brings כרת as חמץ.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא gives a case (dissolved and swallowed bread) where the item fails as מצה but still brings כרת as חמץ. That breaks the claimed match.

steps.title: רב אידי Gives the Real Reason: Fruit Liquids
steps.stepSummary: רב אידי בר אבין wakes up and tells his students that ריש לקיש's real reason is different. Wine, oil, and honey are מי פירות (fruit liquids). His explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אידי בר אבין woke up because of them. He said to them: Children, this is the reason of ריש לקיש: because these are fruit liquids,
steps.whatsHappening: Their teacher, who was dozing in Step 27, wakes up from their discussion. He starts giving a new explanation of ריש לקיש's ruling, and the sentence continues into the next passage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of patching רב פפא's reasoning, רב אידי moves ריש לקיש's reason to a different basis: the type of liquid used. Wine, oil, and honey count as מי פירות. The idea (finished in the next lines) is that these liquids do not create real חמץ that brings כרת. This sidesteps רב הונא's challenge, because the reason no longer depends on the מצה–חמץ link.

keyTerms.meaning: Children; young students (an affectionate, teasing way to address them).
This is the reason. It introduces the true explanation.
Fruit liquids (wine, oil, honey, and similar), as opposed to water.

steps.confusionAlert: This passage stops in the middle of רב אידי's sentence. The full point about what מי פירות do (or don't do) to dough is completed in the next lines.
steps.whyThisMatters: This changes the basis of ריש לקיש's ruling. The question is no longer "can it be מצה?" but "what kind of liquid was used?"

phrases.aramaic: אִיתְּעַר בְּהוּ רַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין,
phrases.english: Rav Idi bar Avin woke up because of them,
and said to them: Children,
this is the reason of Reish Lakish:
because they are fruit liquids,
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּעַר בְּהוּ רַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין, אָמַר לְהוּ: דַּרְדְּקֵי, הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the deadlock created by Step 30. It replaces רב פפא's reasoning with a new reason for ריש לקיש's ruling.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the reasoning: gives a different basis for the original ruling, so the challenge no longer applies.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ריש לקיש's ruling depends on the match between מצה and חמץ (רב פפא).
steps.terutzMaskana: ריש לקיש's ruling depends on the nature of מי פירות (to be completed on the next amud).
